title: If I had known...
goal: Student uses third conditional naturally to express alternative pasts, missed opportunities, and counterfactual scenarios.
connects_to: M14 (Modal perfects: should have, could have, would have) — adjacent regret/speculation forms.

units.title: If I had known
units.grammar_focus: Third conditional structure (If + past perfect, would have + past participle)
units.real_life_context: You imagine alternative pasts — what would have happened differently if you'd had different information.

grammar.sentence: If I _____ known, I would have helped.
grammar.explanation: Third conditional: "If + past perfect (had + past participle), would have + past participle". The "if" clause uses past perfect, even in third conditional. Here: "If I had known".

grammar.sentence: She _____ called you if she had had time.
grammar.explanation: Main clause: "would have + past participle". "She would have called" — not "would call" (that would be second conditional, present).

grammar.sentence: If we _____ left earlier, we wouldn't have missed the train.
grammar.explanation: "If + past perfect" — "had left". The contrast with "wouldn't / would not have missed" reveals the third conditional.

grammar.sentence: I _____ told you if I had known.
grammar.explanation: The main clause always takes "would have + past participle". "I would have told you".

grammar.sentence: If she _____ studied, she would have passed.
grammar.explanation: "If she had studied" — past perfect in the if-clause. She would have passed, but she didn't study.

grammar.sentence: He _____ have come if you had invited him.
grammar.explanation: "He would have come" — would + have + come. Full structure of the main clause.

grammar.sentence: If they _____ asked, I would have helped.
grammar.explanation: "If they had asked" — past perfect in the if-clause of the third conditional. The main clause keeps "would have + past participle".

grammar.sentence: If I would have known, I would have helped.
grammar.hint: "Would" não vai na cláusula "if" — só past perfect
grammar.answer: If I had known, I would have helped.
grammar.explanation: Very common error: using "would have" in the if-clause. In third conditional, "if" always takes past perfect ("had known"), never "would have".

grammar.sentence: She would called you if she had had time.
grammar.answer: She would have called you if she had had time.
grammar.explanation: The main clause needs "would HAVE + past participle". "Would called" doesn't exist — always "would have called".

grammar.passage: If I had known about the meeting, I would have come prepared. She would have called you back if she had had your number. We wouldn't have missed the train if we had left ten minutes earlier.
grammar.question: What would the speaker have done if they had known?
grammar.explanation: The text says "If I had known... I would have come prepared".

listening_speaking.text: If I had known, I would have helped.
She would have called if she had had time.
We wouldn't have missed the train if we had left earlier.
He would have come if you had invited him.
If they had asked, I would have said yes.

units.title: I wish I had
units.grammar_focus: Wishes about the past (I wish + past perfect) — regret
units.real_life_context: You express deep regret about past actions or non-actions.

grammar.sentence: I wish I _____ studied harder.
grammar.explanation: "I wish + past perfect" for regrets about the past. "I wish I had studied" — it's done and I regret it.

grammar.sentence: She wishes she _____ told him the truth.
grammar.explanation: Wish + past perfect for a past regret. "She wishes she had told" — she didn't say it and regrets it.

grammar.sentence: I wish I _____ taken that opportunity.
grammar.explanation: "I wish I had taken" — past perfect for regret over not seizing the chance.

grammar.sentence: He wishes he _____ called you back.
grammar.explanation: "He wishes he had called" — past perfect marking a past action that didn't happen.

grammar.sentence: I wish I _____ listened to my parents.
grammar.explanation: "Wish + past perfect" for regret. "I wish I had listened" — I didn't listen, and I regret it.

grammar.sentence: We wish we _____ left earlier.
grammar.explanation: "We wish we had left earlier" — regret about when we left.

grammar.sentence: If only I _____ known.
grammar.explanation: "If only" = emphatic version of wish. "If only I had known" — dramatic regret.

grammar.sentence: I wish I would have studied harder.
grammar.hint: Use past perfect "had studied", não "would have"
grammar.answer: I wish I had studied harder.
grammar.explanation: Common error: "wish + would have". For the past, use "wish + past perfect" ("had studied"). "Would have" doesn't fit.

grammar.sentence: She wishes she has told him.
grammar.answer: She wishes she had told him.
grammar.explanation: "Has told" (present perfect) doesn't work in wish. For the past, always past perfect "had told".

grammar.passage: I wish I had studied harder in college. She wishes she had taken that job offer. If only we had left earlier — we wouldn't have missed the flight.
grammar.question: What does she wish she had done?
grammar.explanation: The text says "She wishes she had taken that job offer".

listening_speaking.text: I wish I had studied harder.
She wishes she had taken the offer.
If only we had left earlier.
He wishes he had called you back.
I wish I had listened to my parents.

units.title: What would you have done?
units.grammar_focus: Questions in third conditional (Would you have + past participle + if?)
units.real_life_context: You ask hypothetical past questions to explore decisions and alternative outcomes.

grammar.sentence: What _____ you have done if you had known?
grammar.explanation: Third-conditional question: "WH + would have + past participle + if + past perfect?". "What would you have done?" — hypothetical question about the past.

grammar.sentence: _____ you have helped if I had asked?
grammar.explanation: "Would + subject + have + past participle + if + past perfect?". "Would you have helped?" — yes/no third-conditional question.

grammar.sentence: Where would you have gone if you _____ had the money?
grammar.explanation: "If you had had the money" — past perfect auxiliary "had" in the if-clause of the third conditional.

grammar.sentence: If you _____ been there, what would you have said?
grammar.explanation: "If you had been there" — past perfect "had been" in the if-clause of the third conditional.

grammar.sentence: What would you have done if you _____ been in my place?
grammar.explanation: "If you had been in my place" — past perfect in the if-clause for a hypothetical past situation.

grammar.sentence: Would she have called you if she _____ known your number?
grammar.explanation: "If she had known your number" — past perfect in the if-clause of a yes/no third-conditional question.

grammar.sentence: How would you have reacted if it _____ happened to you?
grammar.explanation: "If it had happened to you" — past perfect "had + past participle" in the if-clause.

grammar.sentence: What you would have done if you had known?
grammar.hint: Inversão em pergunta — "would" antes do sujeito
grammar.answer: What would you have done if you had known?
grammar.explanation: In a question, "would" comes before the subject ("would you"), not after ("you would"). Inversion is required in WH-questions.

grammar.sentence: Would you helped if I had asked?
grammar.answer: Would you have helped if I had asked?
grammar.explanation: Always "would HAVE + past participle". "Would you helped" doesn't exist.

grammar.passage: What would you have done if you had been in my position? Where would you have gone if you had had unlimited time? Would you have helped me if I had asked?
grammar.question: What hypothetical question is asked about position?
accepts: what would you have done if you had been in my position
grammar.explanation: The text asks "What would you have done if you had been in my position?".

Would you have helped if I had asked?
Where would you have gone if you'd had time?

units.title: What almost happened
units.grammar_focus: Chained third conditional in narrative — stringing multiple "If + past perfect, would have + past participle" to tell stories of close calls and alternate pasts. Negative forms ("wouldn't have", "nothing would have happened").
units.real_life_context: You narrate "what almost happened" — close calls, near misses, and how one small different choice would have changed an entire chain of events.

grammar.sentence: If the driver had braked in time, the accident _____ happened.
grammar.explanation: Third conditional negative result. "Wouldn't / Would not have happened" — main clause uses "wouldn't / would not have + past participle" for an outcome that DIDN'T occur.

grammar.sentence: Nothing _____ wrong if we had followed the plan.
grammar.explanation: "Nothing would have gone wrong" — main clause of third conditional with indefinite subject. Past participle "gone" after "would have".

grammar.sentence: If I hadn't missed the bus, I _____ her.
grammar.explanation: Third conditional with "never" between "would" and "have". A close-call narrative — missing the bus led to meeting her.

grammar.sentence: She wouldn't have found the job if her friend _____ the link.
grammar.explanation: If-clause of the third conditional uses past perfect: "hadn't / had not shared" — the friend's action made the job possible.

grammar.sentence: If I had taken that flight, I _____ been in the storm.
grammar.explanation: Close call narrative. "I would have been in the storm" — main clause of the third conditional. The auxiliary "would have" introduces the hypothetical past result.

grammar.sentence: We wouldn't have made it if the train _____ been delayed.
grammar.explanation: If-clause needs past perfect negative: "hadn't / had not been delayed". Paradoxically, the delay saved them.

grammar.sentence: Nobody would have noticed if she _____ said anything.
grammar.explanation: "If she hadn't / had not said anything" — past perfect negative in the if-clause. Pairs with "nobody would have noticed" in the main clause.

grammar.sentence: If he didn't call me, I wouldn't have known.
grammar.hint: Third conditional precisa de "had + past participle" na cláusula if
grammar.answer: If he hadn't called me, I wouldn't have known.
grammar.explanation: "Didn't / Did not call" is past simple — it doesn't fit in third conditional. Always "hadn't / had not called" (past perfect).

grammar.sentence: If I had left earlier, I would arrive on time.
grammar.hint: Resultado de third conditional sempre "would HAVE + past participle"
grammar.answer: If I had left earlier, I would have arrived on time.
grammar.explanation: "Would arrive" is second conditional (present). Third conditional needs "would have arrived" (past).

grammar.passage: If I hadn't taken the wrong train that morning, I wouldn't have met Sarah. We wouldn't have started talking. And I would never have moved to Berlin. One mistake changed everything.
grammar.question: What would have never happened if the speaker hadn't taken the wrong train?
grammar.explanation: The text says "I would never have moved to Berlin" — close-call narrative chain.

listening_speaking.text: If I hadn't missed the bus, I would never have met her.
Nothing would have gone wrong if we had followed the plan.
We wouldn't have made it without your help.
Nobody would have noticed if she hadn't said anything.
One small change would have ruined everything.

units.title: Past hypotheticals together
units.grammar_focus: Integration of third conditional + wish + past + chained close calls
units.real_life_context: You alternate fluidly between past hypotheticals, wishes, and chained close-call narratives in real conversation.

grammar.sentence: If I _____ known, I would have called you.
grammar.explanation: Pure third conditional. "Had known" + "would have called".

grammar.sentence: I wish I _____ said no.
grammar.explanation: "Wish + past perfect" for regret. "I wish I had said no" — I didn't say it, and I regret it.

grammar.sentence: If she _____ studied harder, she would have passed the exam.
grammar.explanation: Past perfect "had studied" in the if-clause of the third conditional. The main clause keeps "would have + past participle".

grammar.sentence: What would you have done if you _____ been there?
grammar.explanation: Third-conditional question. "If you had been there" — past perfect in the if-clause.

grammar.sentence: We wouldn't have missed the train if we _____ left earlier.
grammar.explanation: "Had left" — past perfect in the if-clause of the third conditional.

grammar.sentence: If only I _____ listened to you!
grammar.explanation: "If only I had listened" — exclamation of regret.

grammar.sentence: Nothing would have gone wrong if we _____ followed the plan.
grammar.explanation: Emphatic negative third conditional. "If we had followed the plan" — past perfect in the if-clause completes the regret narrative.

grammar.sentence: If I would have known, I would have helped.
grammar.answer: If I had known, I would have helped.
grammar.explanation: The "if" clause is always past perfect ("had known"), never "would have known".

grammar.sentence: I wish I would have studied medicine.
grammar.answer: I wish I had studied medicine.
grammar.explanation: "Wish + past perfect" for regret ("I wish I had studied"). "Would have" is wrong in wish.
